blocks.text: Central Abbotsford homes listed and sold, June to October 2026

Central Abbotsford, October 2026. Detached houses: 79 listed at month end and 6 sold in October, a sales ratio of 8% (a buyers’ market). Condos and townhomes: 236 listed at month end and 42 sold in October, a sales ratio of 18% (a balanced market).

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 33 sold over 5 months against an average of 74.0 listed, about 11.2 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was September with 12 sold. Condos and townhomes: 209 sold over 5 months against an average of 262.6 listed, about 6.3 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 51 sold.

faq.a: Enter the primary home address into the SD34 School Locator portal; SD34 school pages state the portal determines the neighbourhood catchment school, and registration starts at the catchment school. Locator runs for two central test addresses: 33130 Bevan Ave returns Godson Elementary → Abbotsford Middle → Abbotsford Senior Secondary, and 32161 Dormick Avenue returns Dormick Park Elementary → Abbotsford Middle → Abbotsford Senior Secondary (SD34 School Locator, mybaragar.com, run 2026-11-01).
faq.q: How are school catchments checked for a Central Abbotsford address?

faq.a: The City Centre Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2913-2019) and Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2920-2019) are listed as adopted neighbourhood plans in the Abbotsford OCP framework, under the city-wide Abbotsforward 2050 Official Community Plan.
faq.q: Which plans govern the central area?

faq.a: City plan boards list Urban 1 – Midrise up to 6 storeys, Urban 2 – Ground Oriented for rowhouses, townhouse, multiplex or duplex housing, and Urban 3 – Infill for single detached dwellings with some ground-oriented duplexes.
faq.q: What housing forms does the Historic Downtown plan allow near the core?

faq.a: The City flood page describes Sumas Prairie as low-lying agricultural land in East Abbotsford, a separate area from the central upland; parcel-level floodplain status for a central address requires a City floodplain map check.
faq.q: Is Central Abbotsford in the Sumas Prairie floodplain?
